title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: Although the system that managed the linking of the First Flame had rung the bells to resurrect the past Lords of Cinder when needed, not all of them have awakened from their resting places. Consequently, once the Flame eventually goes out, at some point these Lords of Cinder from the past will rise again and wander the lands like tiny flames. These beings will possess fragments of the First Flame stored within their bodies in the form of cinders, giving them the powers of the Flame in a world that will be enveloped in Darkness.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, the First Flame is so weakened that Lords of Cinder past are resurrected so that the embers of the First Flame inside them serve as fuel for new Linkings. Prince Lothric, who was raised to become the next Lord of Cinder, refused to Link the First Flame, while three of the resurrected Lords of Cinder refused to be used as fuel, leading to resurrection of several Unkindled in the hopes that one of them might slay the fleeting Lords of Cinder and Lothric, and Link the First Flame.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The are characters who have linked the First Flame throughout the history of the *Dark Souls* universe.

To "link the First Flame" is to reach it, be powerful enough to withstand its power, and rekindle the flame anew; it is done in order to stop the First Flame from withering out and dying, a process that occurs naturally over time and would mean both the end of the Age of Fire and the coming of an Age of Dark. To attempt to link the flame, one must typically reach the kiln built around the First Flame and defeat the empty husk of the previous Lords of Cinders guarding it against those not worthy of its power.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : The Lords of Cinder are beings that have linked the First Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire through the centuries. Although many of these champions have followed the sacrifice of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, not everyone became a Lord of Cinder through heroic deeds or even of free will. One such case is Aldrich, who became a Lord only because he had the strength to become one, despite having obtained such power by devouring an untold number of humans for his own pleasure.

The continuous linking of the Flame eventually culminated in the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who linked the Flame throughout history. This being, although appearing as an empty husk, inherits the abilities of the Lords of Cinders who have come before. It has long existed as the Flame's last defense inside the Kiln, protecting it from Champions attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength.

title: Ludleth of Courland
snippet: When the link of fire was threatened, the Lords of Cinder would be exhumed from their graves to once again serve as kindling for the First Flame. Ludleth was among those resurrected; though unlike the other three Lords, he accepted the call, and took up his throne at Firelink Shrine to await his fate.

title: First Flame
snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
The prince's decision led the system managing the linking of the Flame to resort to an emergency measure: ringing the bells and awakening the Lords of Cinder of the past from their graves, beings who had previously linked the Flame, to unite their cinders and energize the fading Flame. However, most of the awakened Lords of Cinder refused to sacrifice themselves again and returned to their lands, leaving their thrones at the Firelink Shrine empty.

The ringing of the bells would also awaken the Unkindled, who would hunt down the Lords of Cinder and bring their cinders back to Firelink Shrine. Many of these Unkindled attempted to storm the castle to slay Lothric, but were all killed by the royal guards or by his brother Lorian.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: First Flame
snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. Gwyn's clan linked the sacred bonfires that were tied to the Flame to humanity, and shepherded the humans who worshipped them to kindle the flames. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

#They are not shown in the opening cinematic, meaning they were not resurrected when the bell tolled, implying that Lothric never took his throne in the first place.
#Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle wishes for Lothric's soul to be saved by becoming a part of the firelinking ritual, implying again that Lothric never took his throne in the first place.

title: First Flame
snippet:
First Flame -  Dark Souls - storyline - age_of_fire 
 age_of_fire : With the dragons defeated, the Lords took over the world, ruling as Gods from their seat of power in the land of Lordran. It was a prosperous era, and many nations were born. In time, however, the First Flame began to fade, and with it the power of the Gods, leading to an era of decay and the emergence of the Undead Curse. If the Flame were to gutter out completely, it would end the Age of Fire and bring about the Age of Dark.

title: Lothric
snippet: When the royal family realized that Lothric would not improve from his condition, they resorted to repulsive acts in an attempt to obtain a worthy Champion for the linking: the rulers bound the souls of the two princes together with a curse. Although the exact motive behind this act is unknown, it is likely that the rulers intended for Prince Lothric to draw out some of the strength of his elder brother's soul, which could have allowed him to qualify as worthy Ash for the First Flame. It was even said that Lorian willingly submitted to the curse, even as it crippled him. The resulting Soul of the Twin Princes was one worthy of providing kindling for the First Flame, even as the princes were physically incapable of overcoming the obstacles involved in linking the Flame. Unable and unwilling to fulfill their destiny, the princes retreated to their chamber to await the end of the world.

title: Lothric
snippet:
The relations between the two realms soon blossomed into an alliance, formalized by the incorporation of the sword of Lothric, a symbol of that realm, into the insignia of the Blades of the Darkmoon, the predecessors of the Blue Sentinels and the Way of Blue. In practice, the unification of cultural and religious symbols of the kingdoms allowed the usage of transport demons by those bearing the banner of Lothric.

Now in possession of the knowledge provided by the primordial serpents and the ancient gods of Anor Londo, the kingdom of Lothric developed its role in the linking of the Flame, building the Firelink Shrine just outside the city walls, neighbouring the Royal Gardens, in order to guarantee safe and regulated passage to the Kiln of the First Flame. The shrine would once again accept Fire Keepers who assisted Champions that aspired to link the Flame, drawing out the strength of the souls they acquired to aid them in their journey.

It exists as the Flame's last defense inside its Kiln, protecting it from anyone attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength—a role that it has enacted for a very long time, confronting all who entered the Kiln as aspiring Lords.

title: Dark Lord
snippet:
Dark Lord -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : **This section of the lore lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations**

The Dark Lords are beings who were meant to become Lords of Cinder, but refused to link the First Flame and extend the Age of Fire, with the specific intent of bringing forth the Age of Dark (also referred to as an "Age of Man"). Dark Lords, while powerful enough to overcome the trials involved in linking the Flame, apparently don't have to inherit a primordial force (such as the First Flame) in order to be deemed worthy of their title. For instance, if the Chosen Undead chooses to become a Dark Lord, abandoning the power of the First Flame, several primordial serpents will nevertheless bow before their new Lord (including both Kaathe and Frampt), even as the Chosen Undead lacks the extraordinary power granted by the Flame.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince

Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, who was to achieve great things in his life.

title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

 last_days_of_fire : Many millennia—or even more—have gone by, and the linking of the Fire has become a staple in the world. Finally, when the new "Lord of Cinder" Prince Lothric was destined to sacrifice himself to the Flame, he refused and opted to watch the Age of Dark settle. To save the Age of Gods, four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected as Undead, but three of them either sought the Age of Dark, or no longer cared either way. One last contingency plan existed, to awaken the Unkindled, those who had previously failed to prolong the Age of Fire with their sacrifices. Kaathe's will has been reinterpreted by the Sable Church of Londor, who aim for a different Age of Dark than what Kaathe sought; an age ruled by a Lord of Hollows.

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet: When the First Flame once again began to fade and the previous Lords of Cinder refused to serve as kindling again, the Unkindled buried in the Cemetery of Ash were resurrected. The remains of Gundyr's golem became the judge of these potential champions trying to reach Firelink Shrine. However, after his lifetime of service, the fire that was burned into Gundyr by the Coiled Sword had died down, leaving him open to the pus of man overtaking his body. In his final battle, Iudex Gundyr's raging humanity would erupt in a violent outbreak of dark pus, driven by an untamable fury.

title: Ludleth of Courland
snippet:
Sometime before or after linking the Flame, Ludleth was exiled from his country. He then collaborated with Lothric, where he ensured that all Fire Keepers to come would be deprived of their eyes, to prevent them from observing a future without the First Flame. The original eyes were hidden in a version of the Firelink Shrine on the verge of sinking into darkness, where the First Flame was all but extinguished.

Ludleth eventually linked the First Flame, taking pride in sacrificing himself of his own volition and convinced that, if in life he had been only a pygmy, in death he would have been celebrated as a true Lord. However, he also seems to express remorse for his actions, asking to be forgiven.

title: Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: Realizing that Lothric would not improve from his condition, the royal family resorted to repulsive acts in an attempt to obtain a worthy Champion: the rulers bound the souls of the two princes together with a curse. Although the exact motive behind this act is unknown, it is likely that the rulers intended for Prince Lothric to share in the strength of his elder brother's soul, which could have allowed him to qualify as worthy Ash for the First Flame. It was even said that Lorian willingly submitted to the curse, even as it crippled him. The resulting Soul of the Twin Princes was one worthy of providing kindling for the First Flame, even as the princes were physically incapable of overcoming the obstacles involved in linking the Flame.

This led to the resurrection of four Lords of Cinder of the past, whose conjoined, withered embers could kindle the First Flame in Lothric's stead. Aldrich, Saint of the Deep; Yhorm the Giant, the Abyss Watchers, and Ludleth of Courland were expected to sacrifice themselves as kindling once again. When all Lords except Ludleth rejected this duty, the Unkindled too were resurrected as a last resort, who were fated to seek out the Lords (including Prince Lothric) and bring them back to their thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once the cinders of the Lords were restored to their thrones, an Unkindled champion would be bestowed the embers of the First Flame that remained within their cinders, and finally sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to complete their journey.

snippet: Although the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods lasted for centuries, at some point the First Flame began to fade. Gwyn understood that if the Flame went out, the Age of Fire would be succeeded by an Age of Dark, a new order of humans led by a Dark Lord. Fearful of this outcome, the god made a drastic decision: In order to maintain the order of Gods, he would sacrifice himself to link the dying Flame and prolong its life. He trusted none but himself to carry out the sacrifice involved; he thus divided the power of his Lord Soul among the members of his clan and handed down the power of the sun to his children, leaving his firstborn son to inherit his titles. Gwyn also tasked his sons and Frampt with shepherding the humans into following his example, linking the Flame generation after generation, to uphold his Age of Fire, each of them becoming Lords through the process.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Calling it "futile" is a euphemism: the unnatural prolonging of the First Flame's lifespan came with disastrous, if not, downright catastrophical proportions: when the Lords of Cinder started to resurrect, somehow, portions of their countries and homelands were, literally, "teleported" to Lothric, changing the landscape in unpredictable ways.

snippet: Gwyndolin created an illusory image of his sister Gwynevere, to govern through her cherished figure and covering for her departure, taking upon himself to lead what remained of his father's kingdom and the Silver Knights through this illusion, though he didn't attempt to claim the throne for himself. Gwyndolin also collaborated with Kingseeker Frampt to maintain the system and religion created by his father to keep the First Flame and the Age of Fire alive. Together they used the illusion of Gwynevere to seek a worthy champion to link the Flame again, creating a prophecy which they hoped to make self-fulfilling by guiding and manipulating those who passed their various challenges and earned the Lordvessel, a component required to access the Kiln of the First Flame, while also maintaining some semblance of divinity and control over the ancient city.

title: Lothric
snippet: Over time, the ritual of the Linking of the Fire evolved, from a simple temple inside the Royal Gardens to an arena complete with stands, in which Iudex Gundyr's golem would judge those who aspired to become Lords. Countless people throughout the long history of the kingdom came here to take part in the ritual started with Gwyn's sacrifice. All the Fire Keepers who served their purpose of guiding their Champions would be disposed of and dropped inside the Bell Tower of Firelinking Shrine, piling in up in the dozens. Even more were those Champions who tried and failed to link the Flame, becoming the Unkindled, and were buried near the shrine in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard of all those who failed in their task.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Having secured absolute dominion over the world, Gwyn thus began the Age of Fire, a time of prosperity that was characterized by the power of the First Flame and the vision of the Great Lord. Gwyn's clan placed themselves atop the new world order, assuming the role of deities for humans who were their subjects, and Gwyn took the title "god of sunlight". Humans venerated the gods who lived in the city of Anor Londo in the region of Lordran, building an economy and culture around the use of souls, even hunting the descendants of dragons for sport and domesticating some of them. Gwyn left the other two Lords to tend to their own domains: Izalith built her civilization underground where she and her daughters continued to study flame sorcery, and Gravelord Nito remained in the Catacombs to oversee the dead.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: Sometime later, Gwynevere reached Lothric and became the queen of the kingdom, marrying into the bloodline of its monarchs. The goddess resumed her role as a divinity, producing holy water with healing properties and being worshipped by humans as a symbol of fertility and bounty. Her "angelic daughter" Gertrude also became her holy maiden and her healing miracles were taught to her personal knights. During the long tradition of supporting the linking of the Flame by the kingdom of Lothric, the goddess alone cared for the Cemetery of Ash, the resting place for the Unkindled, beings who had failed to link the flame and whose graves saw no visitors.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - background 
 background : To "link the First Flame" is to reach it, be powerful enough to withstand its power, and rekindle the flame anew. The Unkindled were strong enough to overcome the challenges of reaching the Kiln of the First Flame, but lacked the strength needed to withstand the power of the Flame: the primordial Fire burned them to ash, not fueled enough to properly spark anew. These failed champions' remains were entombed in the Cemetery of Ash.

title: Lore
snippet:
Gwyn, in a final effort to save the Age of Fire, marches with a great deal of his army to the Kiln of the First Flame and sacrifices himself to link with the First Flame, turning the Kiln to ash and incinerating his entire army (making them the Black Knights, who later walk Lordran). The attempt is temporarily successful, however, as the Age of Fire was only extended for at least 1000 years. Gwyn became a Hollow and is from then on known as "Gwyn, Lord of Cinder".

The Four Kings became corrupted and were seduced by evil at some point by Kaathe after Gwyn's fall and their servants turned into Darkwraiths. In an effort to stop them New Londo was flooded with all of its population, trapping the Four Kings with their Darkwraiths in the Abyss.

Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

 the_fast_fading_flame_and_the_birth_of_chaos : Gwyn found one day that the First Flame was fading, and that once it had burnt out the Age of Dark would begin.

The Lords feared the Dark, and sought to prolong the Age of Fire. The Witch of Izalith attempted to create a new flame. However, this new Chaos Flame grew out of control and consumed the Witch of Izalith and many of her children, soon forming into a creation known as the Bed of Chaos, which consumed Izalith and mutated most of the Witch of Izalith's remaining children into abominable creatures, while also turning her only son into a volcanic monstrosity. From the Chaos Flame came the race of Demons, against which Gwyn waged war. The Silver Knights that fought in this war were scorched and became the Black Knights.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
** The weapon skill of the Onyx Blade, "Elfriede's Blackflame", states that the blackflame was "born of the similarly-hued flame that smolders within her". Following from the speculation that Unkindled Ones lack the original Flame, this similarly-hued flame possibly hails from a different source, possibly the First Flame itself within the Kiln, the very fire which ended up burning Elfriede.
** Given the Sable Church's affinity with dark miracles, it seems likely that the First Flame would attempt to manifest within its would-be usurper as a derivation from these arts that are powered by the Darkness of humanity.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
With Elfriede at the helm, the Sable Church developed dark miracles, forged specialized weaponry, and trained knights unflinchingly loyal to their cause. The influence of the Sable Church would extend beyond Londor and into other realms via Londor Pale Shades, assassins and knights who served the interests of the Church abroad. At some point, Sir Vilhelm would come under the employ of the three sisters of the Church. He was especially loyal to Elfriede, becoming her steadfast follower and cold-blooded hangman.

Elfriede eventually departed Londor to attempt to link the First Flame. It is uncertain whether she intended to usurp the Flame, realizing Kaathe's vision of an Age of Dark, or wholly abandoned Londor to link the Flame for another purpose. Regardless, she was unable to withstand the Flame's power, and was burned to Ash.

title: Lords

In his fear of the Age of Dark, he sacrificed himself to the First Flame, prolonging the Age of Fire and becoming Lord of Cinder. This act rendered Gwyn Hollow.

At some point, his firstborn son tamed a stormdrake, and allied with the dragon descendants. For this treachery, he was stripped of his godhood and banished (albeit, not by Gwyn), expunged from all records of history.

However, some remnants of her soul manifested again in Drangleic, continuing to exert their influence on the region.

title: Firelink Shrine (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The opening area is a large circular chamber where five great thrones face a central bonfire, the only bonfire guarded by a Firekeeper in the whole game. Each of the five thrones looks different and unique, fitting the Lord of Cinder it is made for: The first draped with a extravagant red cloth and covered in saintly candles; the next plain and lightly decorated; the center is heavily charred with molten streaks and half-melted features; the next is flanked with a number of swords besides it; and the final is much too large for any normal human to sit upon. All of these thrones (save the second) are missing their respective Lords, and thus the Unkindled must find them and force their cinders to be seated.

Below the main entrance is a tunnel that leads to a back chamber. The Shrine Handmaid sells goods here, and Blacksmith Andre smiths goods here. Throughout the journey, the Unkindled can recruit a number of vendors and tutors to get new gear and learn new spells.

snippet: The interpretation of the Dark Lord's role in founding a new world order seems to have varied over time. The "Dark Lord" ending of *Dark Souls I* entails abandoning the First Flame to die out and beginning a new age from naught; the "Usurpation of Fire" ending of *Dark Souls III* however is somewhat different. Many millennia past the time of the Chosen Undead, the Sable Church of Londor, founded by three sisters who were disciples of Kaathe, are searching for a worthy Lord of Men. If the Ashen One cooperates with Yuria, a sister of the Sable Church, they are asked to "usurp the Flame", to "wrest it from its mantle". In doing so, the Ashen One would inherit what little lifeforce remains of the First Flame, and thus become a worthy Lord of Men—that is, a "Lord of Hollows", as it has come to be referred to. title: Sister Friede
snippet: Following Prince Lothric's refusal to link the First Flame, the Unkindled were exhumed from their graves, tasked with hunting down the Lords of Cinder that had refused to serve once again as kindling. Among the resurrected Unkindled was Elfriede, who instead chose to renounce everything, leaving behind her role as leader of the Sable Church, Londor, and even her name, becoming known simply as "Friede". Left without a home, she was eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel, where the forlorn and the outcast were welcomed and found refuge. Friede became the first Ashen One to reside in it, coming to accept the cold of the Painted World and considering it her new home. She discovered that she wanted to "protect" the inhabitants of the Painted World, and thus assumed the precise form that they yearned for: that of their former mistress Priscilla. title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Age of Fire -  Dark Souls - storyline - description 
 description : **WARNING: This entire page lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations to be considered even useful**

The Age of Fire first began after Gwyn and the other Lords defeated the Everlasting Dragons which ended the Age of Ancients. The Age of Fire was unnaturally prolonged when Gwyn sacrificed himself to kindle the First Flame.

When the Chosen Undead talks to Kingseeker Frampt, he will tell them that they are destined to succeed Gwyn. Should the player choose to kindle the First Flame upon the defeat of Gwyn, they will sacrifice themselves as Gwyn did, thus delaying the Age of Dark once more.

Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Gwyn, Nito and The Witch of Izalith used the power procured from the Lord Souls to challenge the Everlasting Dragons for dominion of the world and, with the help of others, were successful in their endeavor.

The Witch of Izalith attempted to recreate her own First Flame by using her Lord Soul, but this resulted in her own demise and the creation of the Bed of Chaos, mother of all Demons, who inherited possession of the Soul.

Bequeathed Lord Soul Shards are fragments of Gwyn's Lord Soul and were bestowed as gifts. One was given to Seath the Scaleless for betraying his own kind. Another was given to the Four Kings when Lord Gwyn recognized their foresight as leaders of New Londo.

title: Ashen One

 lead : The **Ashen One,** also referred to as the **Champion of Ash** or **the Unkindled One,** is the playable character and the protagonist of *Dark Souls III*.

The title of Ashen One is given to the player by the Fire Keeper of Firelink Shrine. The Ashen One is an Unkindled, an Undead who failed to link the First Flame and became ash, who has been raised from their grave, and is tasked with a journey to defeat four Lords of Cinder and return them to their thrones, since the link of the Flame is threatened and the Lords refuse to serve as its fuel once again.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)

 lead : __NOTOC__

There are four **endings to *Dark Souls III***.

All four endings require the Ashen One to first gather the cinders of four great lords to reach the Kiln of the First Flame, where they must defeat the Soul of Cinder. Only the first ending does not require actions beyond strictly the main questline, although it is possible for up to three to be available simultaneously at the Kiln. All endings revolve around the First Flame, symbolized by a special bonfire that can be interacted with upon slaying the Soul of Cinder.

snippet:

 lore : In the Age of Ancients, the Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great and powerful firestorms. At the time, the Witch and her followers were powerful flame sorcerers who lived in the city of Izalith. Blacksmiths of the ancient city crafted powerful weapons using Chaos arts. Thus, during the earliest known ages of the world, Chaos developed its reputation as a powerful force.

Eventually, the Witch of Izalith attempted to duplicate the First Flame. What she instead produced was a twisted being of chaotic fire: the Bed of Chaos, source of all demons. Several of the Witch's daughters were transformed into chaos demons, and her son became the monstrous Ceaseless Discharge.

title: Lords

 the_witch_of_izalith : The Witch used the power of her Lord Soul to weave great storms of fire against the Everlasting Dragons. She passed fragments of this soul to her children, the Daughters of Chaos, and her only son. Like her children, she had ashen skin and blue lips, though she stood much taller than them and seems to be of identical height to the staves her children used for flame sorcery.

As the fires faded, she tried to create a new flame to replicate the First Flame, but it backfired and ended up costing her life, and gave birth to the race of demons. Her children were also corrupted, except for Quelana, who taught a flame manipulating art to a human and became the mother of pyromancy. Many years later, the demons began to die out, as the flame of chaos began to fade much like the First Flame did.

The Witch and her daughters used flame sorcery to challenge the ancient dragons, casting it from catalysts just as soul sorceries were. In the wake of her attempt to recreate the First Flame, the Witch of Izalith and some of her daughters were engulfed in the newly formed Bed of Chaos. The witches mastered the power of the Flame of Chaos and gave birth to the Pyromancy and all knowledge of flame sorcery has since vanished.

Quelana of Izalith, a Daughter of Chaos, managed to flee the catastrophe created by her mother. Quelana, who is credited as one of the "mothers of pyromancy", after escaping from Izalith, teaches her art to a select few students and now resides in Blighttown.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: According to Darkstalker Kaathe, the Chosen Undead, protagonist of *Dark Souls*, is destined to bring about the Age of Dark, as they are the descendant of the Furtive Pygmy, who possessed the Dark Soul and divided it among early humans in the form of Humanity. title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
During the second phase, he can roll and dodge ranged attacks.
The Soul of Cinder has a fifth weapon style that goes unused, involving a greatsword. snippet:
Both the Orb and Arrow Spread attacks are avoidable by hiding behind one of the pillars on either side of the corridor. The Sphere Shot, on the other hand, will go through walls, inflicting full damage if not blocked or avoided. The Orb Spread and Sphere Shot are Magic-based, though, so a shield that can block 100% physical damage and has good Magic resistance, like the Crest Shield, is recommended for this fight.

While devastating, both the Sphere Shot and Arrow Spread attacks have no tracking whatsoever and are easily avoided simply by running diagonally. Gwyn's design and lore seems to have been heavily inspired by Zeus of ancient Greek mythology.
Several aspects of him can also be compared to the Welsh deity Gwyn ap Nudd.
**Gwyn ap Nudd is said to be a warrior with a "blackened face" similar to Gwyn's hollowed flesh, and the King of the "fair folk." The gods of Lordran being a fair folk.
**In Arthurian legends and writings, Gwyn ap Nudd was the ruler of a delightful paradise called the otherworld, or Annwn. Such a place would be similar to Anor Londo during its glory days.
**Additionally, one can make a comparison between Gwyn ap Nudd leading the Wild Hunt in Welsh legend, and the dragon hunts of Gwyn.
"Gwyn" translated from Welsh means "White/Pure" or "Holy".

It is ideal to block the first hit of his combo, and parry the telegraphed second hit. After performing a riposte, the player will have just enough time to Estus heal.

snippet: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin at some point learned of Gwyn's existence and his story but not his name, referring to him merely as the "Lord of Light". He understood how Gwyn altered the natural order and began linking the Flame, which extended the Age of Fire against the course of nature, and he expresses his outrage at Gwyn for making men lesser than their original form as the "Lord of Light" banished Dark and all that stemmed from Humanity with the Darksign, defining it as the "First Sin" committed against humans and their nature.
